name: Social Insurance Number
issuer: Employment and Social Development Canada (Service Canada)
note: Read the Employment Insurance Act (s. 138, as amended 2012): every person in insurable employment, and every self-employed person under Part VII.1, must have a Social Insurance Number; the Employment Insurance Regulations (s. 89, current to the date served): a person must apply to the Commission to be registered within three days of starting work and tell the employer the number within three days, and the employer must ask for it. Read ESDC's Question Period Note SC_JUN2025_003 (received 2025-05-21): the SIN is a nine-digit number used as a file number for federal programs, introduced in 1964, issued through mail, in person, at birth (SIN@Birth) and online (e-SIN). canada.ca, the SIN pages themselves, didn't answer this egress on 2026-10-30 (connections timed out), so the application conditions, the fee and the processing time aren't read. The check digit: src/papers/numbers/checks.ts names the Luhn formula for the SIN from the Canada Revenue Agency's 'Validating a Social Insurance Number', which this research has not read (the archive refused the fetch), so the format names no check until it is. Readings: 'when' is application (SIN@Birth is the parent's application at birth registration); 'who' is workers, the Act's duty; 'needed' is work.

sources.title: Employment Insurance Act (S.C. 1996, c. 23), s. 138
sources.said: Every person employed in insurable employment, and every self-employed person in respect of whom Part VII.1 applies, must have a Social Insurance Number that has been assigned to that person under an Act of Parliament.

sources.title: Employment Insurance Regulations (SOR/96-332), s. 89
sources.said: An employer who hires a person in insurable employment shall ask the employee, within three days after the day on which the employment begins, to inform the employer of their Social Insurance Number. ... Every person who becomes employed in insurable employment shall, within three days after the day on which the employment begins, inform their employer of their Social Insurance Number.

sources.title: Employment and Social Development Canada, Question Period Note SC_JUN2025_003: Social Insurance Number Program – Service Standards (2025-05-21)
sources.said: Introduced in 1964, the Social Insurance Number (SIN) is a nine-digit number used as a file number for a variety of Government of Canada programs and benefits. ... SIN@Birth channel
